title: Worksheet 14: The Invention of the Computer Mouse
topic: The Invention of the Computer Mouse
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: The computer mouse, a device now used every day by billions of people, was invented in the 1960s by an American engineer named Douglas Engelbart. At the time, most people interacted with computers only through text typed on a keyboard, since graphical screens and pointing devices did not yet exist in everyday use. Engelbart wanted to make it easier for people to select and move things on a computer screen, so he designed a small wooden device with two metal wheels on the bottom and a single button on top, connected to the computer by a wire. Because the wire trailed out the back of the device, resembling a tail, Engelbart and his team nicknamed it a "mouse," and the name stuck. Engelbart first publicly demonstrated the mouse in 1968, during a presentation that also introduced other groundbreaking ideas, such as video conferencing and hyperlinks, decades before these tools became common. Although Engelbart's original mouse looked very different from the mice used today, the basic idea, a handheld device used to point and select things on a screen, remains largely the same.

questions.text: The computer mouse was invented in the 1960s by:
What was Engelbart's original mouse made of?
questions.correct: Wood, with two metal wheels and one button

questions.text: According to the paragraph, why was the device nicknamed a "mouse"?
questions.correct: The trailing wire resembled a tail
distractors: It was very small and fast

questions.text: When did Engelbart first publicly demonstrate the mouse?
Besides the mouse, what other groundbreaking ideas were introduced in Engelbart's 1968 presentation?
distractors: The Enigma code and binary numbers
